G-F061.trick: Long bone = longer than it is wide, with a shaft and two knobby ends (even finger bones!).
G-F061.tip: Bone shape is about proportions, not size. Small finger phalanges are still long bones.

G-F062.trick: DIAPHYSIS = the shaft is the "Divider" between the two ends. EPIphysis = the ends on top.
G-F062.tip: Shaft = diaphysis, ends = epiphyses, the flared region between = metaphysis.

G-F063.trick: Osteon = tree rings around a central pipe (the central canal with vessels and nerves).
G-F063.tip: Concentric rings + central canal = osteon = compact bone. Spongy bone has trabeculae instead.

G-F064.trick: Osteocytes live in lacunae ("little lakes") and talk through canaliculi ("little canals").
G-F064.tip: Canaliculi connect osteocytes so they can share nutrients and signals through hard matrix.

G-F065.trick: Growth plate = the "grow zone". Once it turns to bone, the bone can't get longer.
G-F065.tip: After the epiphyseal plate closes, bones can still get thicker, but not longer.

G-F066.trick: Osteo-CLASTS = Clean up / Chew bone. Osteo-BLASTS = Build bone.
G-F066.tip: In remodeling and fracture repair, osteoclasts remove extra callus while osteoblasts lay new bone.

G-F067.trick: Breakfast at 7, lunch at 12, dinner at 5: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar.
G-F067.tip: For number questions, write the real count first (5 lumbar), then do the math (8 − 5 = 3).

G-F068.trick: Skull bones are zipped together by sutures, like stitches in a baseball.
G-F068.tip: Sutures are fibrous joints that barely move. The squamous suture joins temporal and parietal bones.

G-F069.trick: HUMERUS: the only bone in the upper arm (it's "humorous" when you hit your funny bone near it).
G-F069.tip: Arm = humerus. Forearm = radius (thumb side) and ulna (pinky side). Thigh = femur.

G-F070.trick: Bones are a blood factory: red marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets.
G-F070.tip: Skeleton functions: support, protection, movement, blood cell formation, and storage of minerals (calcium, phosphate) and fat (yellow marrow).

C-ch7-overview.trick: AXIAL = the AXIS down your middle: skull, spine, ribs, sternum (plus the hyoid). Limbs and girdles hang off it.
C-ch7-overview.tip: "Does NOT belong" questions: find the one bone that attaches a limb. Girdles (scapula, clavicle, hip bones) are appendicular.

C-ch7-shape.trick: SESAMOID = shaped like a sesame seed, sitting inside a tendon (patella = the big one).
C-ch7-shape.tip: Bone inside a tendon = sesamoid. The kneecap is the classic example.

C-ch7-long-bone.trick: Drill order = Peel, Crust, Center: Periosteum → Compact bone → Medullary cavity.
C-ch7-long-bone.tip: For "in order" questions, picture the drill path from the outside in before reading the options.

C-ch7-marrow.trick: RED marrow = makes blood (RED for blood). YELLOW marrow = fat.
C-ch7-marrow.tip: All blood cell lines failing at once points to red marrow, which lives in spongy bone in adults.

C-ch7-cells.trick: Block the Clasts (Chewers) = less chewing = denser bone.
C-ch7-cells.tip: Many osteoporosis drugs (like bisphosphonates) work by slowing osteoclasts.

C-ch7-compact-spongy.trick: Osteon rings = compact bone = the hard walls of the shaft.
C-ch7-compact-spongy.tip: Compact bone = osteons, thick in the diaphysis. Spongy bone = trabeculae, inside the ends and flat bones.

C-ch7-ossification.trick: ENDOchondral = bone made INSIDE a cartilage model (most bones). INTRAmembranous = flat skull bones and clavicle.
C-ch7-ossification.tip: Cartilage model mentioned? Think endochondral → long bone. Membrane sheet? Think flat skull bone.

C-ch7-growth.trick: Dark band on an X-ray = cartilage plate still open = still growing. Thin white line = done growing.
C-ch7-growth.tip: Epiphyseal plate (kids) vs epiphyseal line (adults). The line is the scar of a closed plate.

C-ch7-factors.trick: Too much GH: Gigantism if Growing (plates open); Acromegaly in Adults (plates closed) = big hands, feet, jaw.
C-ch7-factors.tip: Check whether the growth plates are open. Same hormone excess, different result.

C-ch7-functions.trick: Bone = a calcium bank: deposits when you have extra, withdrawals when blood is low.
C-ch7-functions.tip: "Mineral reservoir" = bone storing or releasing calcium and phosphate to keep blood levels normal.

C-ch7-remodeling.trick: CalciTONin TONes DOWN blood calcium. PTH Pulls calcium out of bone (raises blood calcium).
C-ch7-remodeling.tip: High blood calcium → calcitonin. Low blood calcium → PTH. They do opposite jobs.

C-ch7-fractures.trick: Spiral = twist. Toddlers don't twist their own arm falling off a couch.
C-ch7-fractures.tip: When the injury doesn't match the story, think abuse. Nurses are mandated reporters.

C-ch7-axial.trick: SCOLIOSIS = S-shaped spine (Side curve). Kyphosis = hunchback. Lordosis = swayback.
C-ch7-axial.tip: Uneven shoulders or hips on the forward-bend test = scoliosis. Screening is common in teen girls.

C-ch7-appendicular.trick: Collarbone = clavicle = pectoral girdle = appendicular (it hangs the arm on the body).
C-ch7-appendicular.tip: Girdles attach limbs to the axial skeleton, so they count as appendicular.

C-ch7-aging.trick: Osteoporosis risk: Thin, White, Older Woman after menopause (estrogen loss).
C-ch7-aging.tip: Hip fractures happen in spongy-bone-rich spots like the femoral neck. Estrogen protects bone.
C-ch7-aging.why: Women of White or Asian ancestry tend to start with a lower peak bone mass, and all women lose bone quickly after menopause, when estrogen falls. Your guide (and exam) says 'light-skinned'; skin color itself doesn't weaken bone, it stands in for ancestry. Hip fractures happen where spongy (trabecular) bone is plentiful, such as the femoral neck.

C-ch7-disorders.trick: Rickets = Rickety bowed legs from no sunshine vitamin (D).
C-ch7-disorders.tip: Vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium. Kids → rickets (bowed legs); adults → osteomalacia (soft bones).
